_readme: Courtyard V2 floor — OPTION ROUND. Four full-plate floors to choose a direction from.
BRIEF RESET (Raheem, 2026-08-04). The first attempt (configs/courtyard-v2-floor.json)
made flagstone the anchor and treated seamless tiling as the gate. Both were wrong:
'Think this is an open air castle courtyard. There's no roof over it, it's outside.
There's a fountain in the middle. This place is probably dirt and grass. I just want
really high quality, really nice dirt grass. Like, maybe paths in between the area.'
'We don't gotta make tiles perfectly. We're gonna cover them up with rugs in some
areas. We're gonna put a lot of stuff over them. You don't gotta go so hard on this.
We want beauty. That's why we're coming to Leonardo, not perfect lines.'
So: GRASS AND DIRT IS THE HERO MATERIAL. Stone is at most paths through it. Seams are
no longer a gate — rugs and props cover the floor. Beauty beats tileability.
WHY FULL PLATES, NOT 512 SWATCHES: 1536x1152 matches the plate exactly, so the angle
can be judged directly against the real courtyard instead of inferred from a tile. It
also lets the paths actually be painted radiating from the centre, which is the thing
Raheem asked to see. Tiling constraints bought us nothing once seams stopped mattering.
THE ANGLE IS THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE PERFECT. Raheem, 2026-08-04: 'The thing that
needs to be perfect is the angle, the angle to match the game.'
WHY THE FIRST RUN CAME BACK PLAN VIEW — the important lesson. Its styleHeader asked for
55 degrees AND ALSO said 'no vanishing point, no horizon, constant uniform foreshortening
identical at the top edge and the bottom edge'. Straight-down plan view satisfies every
one of those clauses perfectly. The anti-perspective language made plan view the easiest
correct answer and it outvoted the 55 degrees. Do NOT reintroduce those clauses. The way
to hold parallel projection without inviting plan view is to say the angle stays constant
ACROSS the image, never to negate the horizon — and to give a concrete tell that only an
oblique view produces (you can see a sliver of the front face of things sitting on the
ground; the fountain's rim reads as an ellipse, not a circle).
THE ANGLE CLAUSE WAS NEARLY REINTRODUCED. A first draft of the styleHeader below still
said 'the camera angle stays exactly the same across the whole image, near edge and far
edge alike'. That is the SAME failure reworded without the word 'no' — plan view has zero
foreshortening variance by definition, so it satisfies 'the same everywhere' better than a
real oblique does. environment-art-director caught it before spend, 2026-08-04. The angle
sentence is now anchored to configs/courtyard.json:5 verbatim — the styleHeader that
actually produced courtyard-v2-figma.png, the plate we are matching. It carries no
anti-perspective negation at all, and its walls came back leaning 13/12 degrees. Never
add a 'constant across the image' clause here again; it existed only so a 512 swatch could
tile, and tiling is no longer a gate.
OPTION D IS DEFINED BUT HELD. Stone-dominant paving contradicts the hero-material rule
above, and B already tests stone as paths. It stays in the file only because Raheem said
'I wanna see maybe this stone if we can get it to work' — release it only if he asks.
STILL BINDING FROM THE FIRST CONFIG — do not relax either:
- SHADOWLESS. The whole point of replacing the floor is that the plate's baked diagonal
shadow is a fixed sun, and you cannot animate a light welded into the art. All
lighting moves to Phaser. No cast shadow, no directional light, no vignette.
- PALETTE. COURTYARD_PALETTE.md Layer 2: name the colours or you get neutral grey,
which matches nothing here. Plate paving is 229,202,115 (warm honey). The gate run
proved this works — its stone measured 240,204,136. Every line below names warm
honey-amber / ochre / verdant explicitly.
NO FOUNTAIN IN THESE PLATES. The fountain is a separate object (still undecided: Figma
cut vs PixelLab). These floors leave a clear circular area at the centre for it to sit in.
RUGS SIT ON TOP. sprite-lab/configs/courtyard-rugs.json — one per quadrant. Keep the
ground quiet enough that four loud rugs still read on top of it.
COST: 4 generations, one per option. No anchor reuse — each is a distinct direction, so
they are deliberately independent.

styleHeader: Painterly hand-painted fantasy environment art, digital matte painting, soft blended brushwork, storybook warmth, cinematic depth, high-angle oblique view looking down at roughly 55 degrees — the camera of a classic Pokemon or JRPG overworld town, tilted enough that anything resting on the ground would show a sliver of its front face and any circle drawn on the ground reads as a wide ellipse rather than a true circle. This is emphatically NOT a straight-down plan view or a map. Lush, beautiful, richly painted outdoor ground in a sunny open-air castle courtyard with no roof: gorgeous colour, generous natural variation, nothing mechanical or repeating. Flat even shadowless ambient daylight spread uniformly across the entire surface, as if lit from everywhere at once — no single light source, no highlight, no glare, no vignette darkening at the corners. Ground surface only, filling the frame edge to edge.

familyLabels.options: Courtyard V2 floor — direction options (full plate, Lucid Origin)

states.label: A — Grass and dirt, no stone
states.line: The open-air courtyard ground is entirely living grass and bare earth, with no paving and no stone anywhere. Deep verdant sunlit turf, richly painted with real blade texture, clover and small wildflower tufts. Broad soft desire-paths of warm honey-amber and ochre-brown packed earth, worn through the grass by generations of feet, radiate from a bare circular patch of earth at the centre of the courtyard out toward each edge, their borders soft where turf frays into soil. Beautiful, natural, hand-painted, no hard lines.

states.label: A2 — A at high noon, ground only (Raheem's shadow fix)
states.line: It is exactly high noon with the sun straight overhead, so nothing casts any shadow in any direction and the light is perfectly even everywhere. Open courtyard ground fills the whole frame corner to corner, with nothing standing on it and nothing at its edges — no walls, no hedges, no trees, no boulders, no timber. Deep verdant sunlit turf with real blade texture and clover. Broad soft paths of warm honey-amber and ochre packed earth, worn by generations of feet, radiate from a bare circular patch of earth at the centre out to each edge. Beautiful, natural, hand-painted.

states.label: V1 — Vast courtyard, grass and dirt (cut the middle)
states.line: An immense castle courtyard seen from far above. The open ground stretches unbroken right across the whole frame, and the surrounding wall is only a thin strip along the extreme outer edge, tiny against all that ground. The sun is nearly overhead, so what little shadow the wall casts hugs the base of the wall itself and never reaches out across the open ground, which is evenly lit everywhere. Deep verdant sunlit turf with real blade texture and clover, and broad soft paths of warm honey-amber and ochre packed earth worn across it. Beautiful, hand-painted.

states.label: V3 — Open courtyard, grass leading, no paths
states.line: An immense castle courtyard of open ground seen from far above, with nothing laid across it and nothing standing on it. The surrounding wall is only a thin strip at the extreme outer edge, and the sun is nearly overhead so the wall's shadow hugs its own base and never reaches the open ground. Deep verdant sunlit turf richly painted with blade texture, clover and tiny wildflowers, mingling in soft organic patches with bare warm honey-amber and ochre packed earth worn bare by generations of feet. Beautiful, hand-painted.

states.label: V4 — Open courtyard, earth leading, no paths
states.line: An immense castle courtyard of open ground seen from far above, with nothing laid across it and nothing standing on it. The surrounding wall is only a thin strip at the extreme outer edge, and the sun is nearly overhead so the wall's shadow hugs its own base and never reaches the open ground. A broad sweep of bare warm honey-amber and ochre packed earth, richly painted with fine granular texture and faint scuffs, with drifts of deep verdant sunlit turf and clover surviving in soft organic patches across it. Beautiful, hand-painted.

states.label: V2 — Vast courtyard, grass, dirt and stone paths
states.line: An immense castle courtyard seen from far above. The open ground stretches unbroken right across the whole frame, and the surrounding wall is only a thin strip along the extreme outer edge, tiny against all that ground. The sun is nearly overhead, so what little shadow the wall casts hugs the base of the wall itself and never reaches out across the open ground, which is evenly lit everywhere. Deep verdant turf and warm ochre packed earth, crossed by wide paths of uneven warm honey-amber stone slabs, never grey, with grass between them. Beautiful, hand-painted.

states.label: B — Grass and dirt with stone paths
states.line: The open-air courtyard ground is mostly deep verdant sunlit grass and warm honey-amber packed earth, crossed by old stone walkways. Wide paths of irregular warm honey-amber and cream sunlit stone slabs, never neutral grey, run outward from a circular stone ring around the bare centre of the courtyard toward each edge, the slabs uneven in size and shape and softened by age, with moss and grass creeping up between them. Between the paths lie generous beds of rich green turf and patches of bare ochre soil where feet cut the corners. Beautiful, natural, hand-painted, no hard lines.

states.label: C — Packed earth courtyard, grass at the edges
states.line: The open-air courtyard ground is mostly bare packed earth, a wide sweep of warm honey-amber and ochre-brown compacted soil, never neutral grey, richly painted with fine granular texture, faint hairline cracks, shallow scuffs and a few small pebbles pressed flat. Broad soft sweeping arcs of tone show where feet have crossed and recrossed it. Deep verdant grass survives in generous drifts around the outer edges and in the corners, fraying softly into the earth where the two meet. Beautiful, natural, hand-painted, no hard lines.

states.label: D — Stone retry, organic and irregular (not gridded)
states.line: The open-air courtyard ground is old cobbled paving, laid in loose organic swirls and fans that curve outward from a circular ring at the centre of the courtyard, deliberately never a grid and never in straight rows. The stones vary enormously in size and shape, from wide flat slabs to small rounded cobbles, all in warm honey-amber, cream and soft ochre sunlit stone, never neutral grey, worn smooth and uneven with age. Deep green moss and grass grow thickly in the wide joints between them, and whole patches of paving have given way to bare soil and turf. Beautiful, natural, hand-painted, no hard lines.
